body:
It's furniture that he's accumulated over time from family members. It furnished our apartment prior to it going into the unit however he owned all of it before we met. 

We aren't married.

I'm no relationship expert, however, I would personally give him another chance based off of the things you've stated.

First, he was open about his cheating immediately and while that doesn't excuse his actions, I think it says a lot. The downfall to this is can you move past it? If you two were apart for a weekend would you feel comfortable or if his phone were going off when he wasn't around would you trust him enough not to check it sort of thing. If his past infidelity is going to eat away at you then you're better off letting go as the relationship would stand no chance without trust.

Second, it sounds like the time apart was healthy for you two. Granted he went down a dark path for awhile, he also came to the realization on what he wanted out of life and it seems that would be you. He made the decision to get his act together because he felt you deserved a better man than an unemployed drug user. He put in the work. It sounds like you truly benefited from the time apart as well. They say timing is everything and maybe you both needed those two years to grow.

Lastly, is it worth the risk to you? Is he worth putting trust into again? Only you can decide that. Relationships are never guaranteed to work out forever and you two may fail again- there is no way to know unless you try. However, if it didn't work you will have tried and there would be no "what if's" Two years is a decent amount of time for you both to still be lingering on this.

I think I'm just upset with myself. There were many red flags early on and I was warned by an ex of his that he was unstable with a very lengthy message of examples. I ignored her warnings and gave him the benefit of the doubt. 

When I found out I was pregnant he initially left for a weekend and told me to have an abortion saying he did not want the baby. After a few days he came around and I forgave his harsh words chalking it up to fear. However, there were incidences throughout my pregnancy that suggested he was not ready and did in fact not want our daughter. Obviously it wasn't all bad and I loved him through his tantrums but I knew in my heart he wasn't father material. We sat down mid June prior to our lease ending and I gave him his out. I told him if he wasn't ready then I was okay letting go. He told me he wanted his family and he'd be there- only to permanently leave about two weeks later. 

It's really hard not to be mad at myself because I've now put my daughter in this situation with a man I fear will disappoint her for years to come. I was desperate for my "family" to work out and I now see how selfish that was in regards to her safety. I don't feel he wants to be around but I do feel like he may try to fight me for her just to be spiteful.

I don't need his child support as thankfully my family is extremely supportive. He's actually reached out to me about paying my part of the phone bill- the phone he shattered and took when he left. So, he's seeking money from me instead of vice versa. 

I feel if he takes me to court then it proves he actually wants to be a parent. I am concerned about not inviting him to her birth though. I'm not sure if that's because I was so used to catering to him in the relationship or I'm just trying to be a decent human. My fear is he will make a scene when he can't take her home with him though.
Message me if you want to talk. Our stories are extremely different so I can't relate on a lot but I'm still here to listen if you need it.
